name: describe_dataset
when_to_use: Call it first on any new DataFrame. It reports the shape, each column's dtype, missing and distinct counts and memory, the index and the provenance you supply, and flags structural problems: empty data, duplicated or colliding column labels, MultiIndex columns, a non-unique index, all-missing columns and constant columns. Every other analysis raises on bad column labels, so run this one to find them. It never shows a raw data value. A dtype only tells how pandas stores a column: to learn each column's logical type from its values, call `infer_column_semantics` next. For missing values per column and per row, call `profile_missing_values`; for how numeric values are distributed, `summarize_numeric`.
signature: describe_dataset(data: pd.DataFrame, *, source: str | None = None, source_version: str | None = None) -> DescribeDatasetResult

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: The data to describe. Any column labels are accepted, including duplicated ones and MultiIndex columns. It is never modified.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Where the data came from, such as a file path, URL or table name, recorded exactly as given. None, the default, records the source as not supplied; it is never inferred.

parameters.name: source_version
parameters.description: The version of the source, such as a snapshot date or a commit, recorded exactly as given. None, the default, records it as not supplied.

source.title: Source
source.description: Where the data came from, such as a file path, URL or table name, recorded exactly as given. None, the default, records the source as not supplied; it is never inferred.

source_version.title: Source Version
source_version.description: The version of the source, such as a snapshot date or a commit, recorded exactly as given. None, the default, records it as not supplied.

statuses.reason: The description finished, also for data with no rows, no columns or neither; a count that can't be computed is null, with a limitation.

finding_codes.description: suspected; the data has no rows, no columns or neither.
suspected; a column label occurs more than once.
suspected; different labels share a string form, such as 1 and '1'.
suspected; the column labels form a MultiIndex.
suspected; index labels repeat, so they don't identify rows.
suspected; a column holds only missing values.
suspected; a column holds a single distinct non-missing value in at least two rows; NaN is missing.

limitation_codes.meaning: Values can't be hashed, so counts of distinct values are null. Lists and dicts are such values.
A key search left out float columns that hold fractions. They are measurements rather than IDs, and the default columns don't select them.
A statistic needs more values than the column has, so it is null. A standard deviation of one value is an example.
Every value is equal, so a statistic such as skewness is null.
Numbers beyond ±2^53 were read as float64, which rounds them. Integers and decimals are such numbers.
Booleans were read as numbers: 0 for False and 1 for True.
A column stores NaN as a value, which every analysis counts as missing, unlike isna().
A categorical column has one level per row of a pair, so its value is null.
A computation overflowed or failed, so the values it affects are null. Division by zero, an invalid value and precision loss are examples; the fields are empty when no value could be named.
Index labels or id_column values repeat, so a row ID can match several rows.
No sentinel values were declared, so counts are null or candidates stay suspected. Stand-ins such as -999 don't count as missing.
A ranking stopped at its work limit before it was proven. An uncounted set could outrank a listed one.
No expected labels were declared, so labels outside them weren't checked. The fields that list those labels are null.
No rare_share was declared, so rare classes weren't checked. The fields that list them are null.
A declared column isn't in the data, so its dtype and counts are null.
No schema was declared, so no column was compared with a declared type. The fields that hold the comparison are null.
nullable wasn't declared for a column, so its missing values weren't checked and its nullable field is null.
A column has no inferred logical type, so the field is null. No value is left after the missing ones, or none fits.
A field belongs to the other task, so it is null. The tasks are classification and regression.

result_fields.name: column_level_count
result_fields.description: Levels in the column labels: 1, or more for MultiIndex columns.

result_fields.name: memory_bytes
result_fields.description: Bytes the columns and the index use together.

result_fields.name: columns
result_fields.description: One entry per column, in DataFrame order: a list, not a mapping by name, because column labels can repeat. The record keeps the first 100 and adds columns_total; the complete table has every column.

fields.name: position
fields.description: 0-based position of the column in the data.

fields.name: column
fields.description: The column label as a string.

fields.name: label_type
fields.description: Python type of the column label, such as 'str', 'int' or 'tuple'. Select a column whose label isn't a str with its original label.

fields.name: dtype
fields.description: The dtype as pandas reports it, such as 'int64'.

fields.name: non_missing_count
fields.description: Values that are not missing.

fields.name: missing_count
fields.description: Native missing values: NaN, NaT and the missing markers of object, nullable and pyarrow-backed columns, including NaN that a pyarrow-backed or nullable float column stores as a value, which pandas' missing-value check doesn't count.

fields.name: distinct_count
fields.description: Distinct non-missing values; null when the values can't be hashed, with an unhashable_values limitation.

fields.name: memory_bytes
fields.description: Bytes the values use, counting each object a text or object column holds. Excludes pandas' lookup tables and the UTF-8 copy Python caches inside a string once something has encoded it, so earlier work on the data doesn't change it.

fields.name: dtype
fields.description: The index dtype as pandas reports it.

fields.name: level_count
fields.description: Index levels: 1, or more for a MultiIndex.

fields.name: is_unique
fields.description: Whether every index label occurs once.

fields.name: duplicated_count
fields.description: Labels that repeat an earlier label.

fields.name: missing_count
fields.description: Missing labels; in a MultiIndex, labels with any level missing.

fields.name: memory_bytes
fields.description: Bytes the index labels use. Excludes pandas' lookup tables and the UTF-8 copies Python caches inside strings.

fields.name: source
fields.description: The source as supplied, or null when not supplied. Never inferred.

fields.name: source_version
fields.description: The source version as supplied, or null when not supplied.

fields.name: not_supplied
fields.description: Provenance fields the caller did not supply.

shared_result_fields.name: analysis
shared_result_fields.description: Name of the analysis, such as 'describe_dataset'.

shared_result_fields.name: method
shared_result_fields.description: The method used, or null when the analysis has no methods.

shared_result_fields.name: status
shared_result_fields.description: How the run ended. Each analysis's Statuses: section lists the ones it can return and why. It says nothing about whether the data passed a check.

shared_result_fields.name: status_reason
shared_result_fields.description: Why the run didn't complete; null when status is completed.

fields.name: code
fields.description: Stable code from the package-wide list, StatusReasonCode. Each analysis's Statuses: section names the codes it returns.

fields.name: message
fields.description: One sentence on what happened.

shared_result_fields.name: parameters
shared_result_fields.description: The resolved arguments by name, defaults included. data appears only as its row_count and column_count, and project whole. In the record, a list or mapping argument keeps its first 100 entries and gains <name>_total; a list inside a mapping argument keeps its first 100 entries too, and gains <key>_total beside it when it lost some. The record writes an integer beyond ±2^53 as a string.

fields.name: row_count
fields.description: Rows in the data given to the analysis.

fields.name: column_count
fields.description: Columns the analysis selected.

fields.name: columns
fields.description: The selected columns where something was excluded, in the selected order. A column not listed had every row eligible and evaluated: eligible_count and evaluated_count equal row_count, and excluded_count is 0.

fields.name: column
fields.description: The column label as a string.

fields.name: eligible_count
fields.description: Values eligible for the analysis.

fields.name: evaluated_count
fields.description: Values the analysis evaluated.

fields.name: excluded_count
fields.description: Eligible values left out.

fields.name: excluded_by_reason
fields.description: Excluded values per reason: missing, infinite, unexpected_label, unhashable_values or too_many_categories.

fields.name: code
fields.description: Stable code naming the kind of finding.

fields.name: claim
fields.description: One sentence from a fixed template.

fields.name: assessment
fields.description: descriptive: a neutral fact. suspected: a possible problem to judge. violation: the data breaks something declared. passed: a declared check held. unknown: a declared check couldn't be evaluated.

fields.name: columns
fields.description: The columns the finding concerns.

fields.name: fields
fields.description: Paths of the result fields behind the claim, such as 'columns[2].missing_count'. A mapping entry is named by its key, as in columns['age'], and a pair by its two columns, as in pairs['age', 'income']. In the record, every path resolves.

shared_result_fields.name: limitations
shared_result_fields.description: What limits how far the result can be read.

fields.name: code
fields.description: Stable code from the package-wide list, LimitationCode.

fields.name: reason
fields.description: One sentence on what is limited and why.

fields.name: fields
fields.description: Paths of the result fields it affects.

shared_result_fields.name: execution
shared_result_fields.description: Library versions used for the run.

fields.name: versions
fields.description: Versions of agent_eda, Python and every library the analysis used, keyed by import name.

>>> import pandas as pd
>>> import agent_eda as ae
>>> df = pd.DataFrame(

...         "age": [34, 51, 29, 51],
...         "score": [0.5, None, 0.75, 0.5],

>>> res = ae.describe_dataset(df, source="survey.csv")
